requirements.requirement: node1 has a routed address on each of its two segments (eth1, eth2)
requirements.summary: eth1 assigned 172.20.1.1/24 and eth2 assigned 172.20.2.1/24 with per-interface and global IPv4 forwarding enabled, confirmed both pre-restart and post-restart.

requirements.requirement: working path between node2 and node3 via node1
requirements.summary: node2 (172.20.1.2/24) and node3 (172.20.2.2/24) configured with static routes via node1's segment addresses; bidirectional ping succeeded with 0% loss both before and after node1's restart.

requirements.requirement: configuration returns automatically after node1 is restarted, with node2/node3 reachability restored
requirements.summary: Full disruption cycle directly observed: healthy pre-restart baseline (boot_id e5168e03..., eth1/eth2 addresses, ip_forward=1) captured, restart acknowledged, a different post-restart boot_id (5efc5171...) confirms a real reboot, and post-restart state shows eth1/eth2 addresses, all forwarding sysctls, and the persisted config files (/etc/network/interfaces.d/60-antrieb-segments, /etc/sysctl.d/99-antrieb.conf) restored automatically without manual intervention, with node2<->node3 ping succeeding with 0% loss in both directions afterward.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct evidence: node1 received routed addresses on both segments (eth1 172.20.1.1/24, eth2 172.20.2.1/24) with forwarding enabled, node2 and node3 achieved a working bidirectional path through node1, and a full restart transition (pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot_id, post-restart config recovery, and restored node2<->node3 reachability) confirms the configuration persists across reboot without manual intervention. The only notable hygiene issue was an unnecessary but bounded and self-reverting mutation to node1's docker0 interface unrelated to the task.
limitations: node2 and node3 were not restarted as part of this task, so no restart/recovery evidence exists for them; this is consistent with the task instruction scoping the restart to node1 only and does not affect the material outcomes.

Persistence relies on SONiC regenerating /etc/network/interfaces from a template that sources /etc/network/interfaces.d/*, which was directly confirmed working via the observed post-reboot state, but the underlying template mechanics were not independently audited beyond the executor's inspection of interfaces-config.sh.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most executor mutations (eth1/eth2 addressing, forwarding sysctls, persistence files, NetworkManager static routes on node2/node3) were directly required for the stated outcomes. One mutation had no clear necessity: cmd-f6ce015b9bc7441b flushed and set down node1's unrelated docker0 interface (240.127.1.1/24) as a precautionary 'SONiC gotcha' cleanup, even though docker0 has no bearing on eth1/eth2 segment routing. This was bounded and low-risk, and SONiC's own config regeneration restored docker0's original address and up/down state after the reboot (visible in cmd-1dcad3fabc9e48dc), so no lasting residue remained. No abandoned files, conflicting/failed services introduced (system-health.service and watchdog-control.service were already failed before the task, unchanged after), unsafe exposure, or damaged package state were observed; dpkg package-health remained consistent before and after.
